title: 5 Financial Mistakes to Avoid Before Filing for Divorce in Colorado

content.rendered:
Deciding to file for divorce is never easy. Along with the emotional challenges, there are important financial decisions that can have a lasting impact on your future. Taking time to prepare before filing can help you avoid common mistakes and put you in a better position as you move through the legal process.

If you’re considering divorce in Colorado, here are five financial mistakes to avoid before filing.

1. Failing to Gather Financial Documents

One of the most common mistakes people make is waiting until after the divorce process begins to organize their financial information. Gathering important documents in advance can make the process more efficient and help you better understand your financial situation.

Consider gathering important financial documents, including recent pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, retirement account information, mortgage documents, credit card statements, and records of any significant assets or debts. Having this information readily available can also help your attorney better evaluate your case.

2. Making Major Financial Decisions Too Soon

It’s understandable to want to make changes when you’re preparing for divorce, but making major financial decisions too early can create unnecessary complications.

For example, transferring money, selling property, opening new credit accounts, or making large purchases without understanding the legal implications may affect your case. Before making significant financial changes, it’s often beneficial to speak with an experienced family law attorney.

3. Focusing Only on Assets Instead of Debts

When people think about divorce, they often focus on who will receive certain assets. However, debts are also an important part of the financial picture.

Mortgages, credit cards, personal loans, vehicle loans, and other financial obligations may all need to be addressed during the divorce process. Understanding both your assets and liabilities can help you make more informed decisions as your case moves forward.

4. Not Planning for Your Financial Future

Divorce often brings significant financial changes. Creating a realistic budget before filing can help you prepare for future expenses, including housing, insurance, transportation, childcare, and other day-to-day costs.

Taking a proactive approach allows you to better understand your financial needs and identify any adjustments that may be necessary after the divorce is finalized.

5. Waiting Too Long to Speak With a Family Law Attorney

Many people delay speaking with an attorney because they’re still deciding whether divorce is the right option. However, scheduling a consultation doesn’t mean you’ve made a final decision—it simply gives you the opportunity to understand your rights and your legal options.

An experienced family law attorney can answer your questions, explain the divorce process in Colorado, and help you avoid common mistakes before filing.

Preparing Today Can Help You Tomorrow

Every divorce is unique, and no two situations are exactly alike. Preparing financially before filing for divorce can help reduce uncertainty and make the process easier to navigate.

If you’re considering divorce in Colorado, speaking with an experienced family law attorney can help you better understand your options and make informed decisions about your future.
